chunks: And Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal narrated from Thalabah ibn Maymun from Muawiyah ibn Ammar, who said:
I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man who bequeathed a portion of his wealth, so he said: 'A portion is one-tenth.'
Allah, the Almighty, said: 'Then place on every mountain a portion of them,' and the mountains were ten.
ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic legal definition of a 'portion' (juz') in a will or bequest?
ai.summary: Imam Al-Sadiq (as) establishes the legal definition of a 'portion' (juz') in bequests as one-tenth, grounding this ruling in the Quranic narrative of Prophet Ibrahim (as) who was instructed to place a portion on each of ten mountains. This interpretation by Shaykh al-Saduq in *Man La Yahduruhu al-Faqih* highlights the exegetical link between the specific numerical mention of 'ten mountains' and the fractional share, providing a clear scriptural basis for calculating bequests in Shia jurisprudence.
